sentences.show: He was shot in the face, the head, the stomach, the ankle, the leg, the hip and the ear. He wrote: "Frankly, I had enjoyed the war."
His name was Adrian Carton de Wiart. And he might be the hardest man in British history.
At 19, he dropped out of Oxford, lied about his name and age, and went to fight in South Africa. He was shot in the stomach.
In 1914, in Somaliland, he was shot twice in the face. He lost his left eye.
Then he went to the Western Front.
In 1915, his left hand was shattered. When the doctor refused to cut off his fingers, he pulled them off himself.
At the Somme, he was shot through the skull. At Passchendaele, the hip. Then the leg. Then the ear.
In 1916, when three other commanders went down, he took over all their men, and held the line. He won the Victoria Cross.
In the next war, he was in his sixties. His bomber crashed into the sea off Libya.
He swam ashore, and was captured by the Italians.
He tried to escape five times, and once spent seven months digging a tunnel.
He stayed free for eight days, disguised as a peasant. With one eye, one hand, and not a word of Italian.
He died peacefully in Ireland, at 83.
One historian described him as "an elegant pirate". With a black eye patch, and an empty sleeve.
Adrian never gave up. Don't give up on history. Subscribe.
